This is the first of a monthly series on what has changed in the development
version of `tidycreel`. CRAN releases come about every two months, and the
development version on GitHub gets fixes and features in between. These posts
are for anyone who wants to know what is coming before it reaches CRAN, and in
particular **whether it changes your numbers**.

The current CRAN release is 8.0.0. Since then, the development version has
gained about a hundred entries in its
[NEWS](https://chrischizinski.com/tidycreel/dev/news/). This post does not
cover them all. It covers the ones that change an estimate or a standard error,
and the ones that change what you see when you run your code.

To try the development version:

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("chrischizinski/tidycreel")
```

## The default total is now the season total

This is the change most users will notice first.

`estimate_effort()`, `estimate_total_catch()`, `estimate_total_harvest()` and
`estimate_total_release()` used to default to `target = "sampled_days"`: the
total over the days that were actually counted. They now default to
`target = "period_total"`: the total for the season. Both printed as
"Method: Total", so a default call on a partly sampled season quietly reported
a fraction of it. On the package's example season, 36 of 120 days were sampled,
and the default effort was 3,066 angler-hours against a season total of 9,994.

Every default total on a design that did not sample every day changes. To get
the old numbers, ask for them by name with `target = "sampled_days"`.

A related check: `add_counts()` now warns when every day of every stratum has a
count. The calendar is the population of days, so a calendar built from only
the sampled dates turns the design into a census, and the season total becomes
the effort of those days alone. In one example that was 2,380 angler-hours
against 8,651 for the full 61-day season, with nothing said. If you see this
warning, pass the full season calendar to `creel_design()`.

## Estimates that change

These fixes move point estimates, not just standard errors.

- **Aerial catch, harvest and release totals were too small.** They were
  computed from the raw instantaneous count rather than from effort, so they
  missed the `h_open`, angler-ratio and visibility scaling that
  `estimate_effort()` applies: 14 times too small with `h_open = 14`. **If you
  have reported aerial totals from 8.0.0, re-run them.**
- **Refused interviews were used as real trips.** `add_interviews(refused =)`
  stored the flag, but no estimator read it, so a refused party usually entered
  the rate with a catch of 0. Flagging 10 interviews as refused on the example
  data took the catch rate from 2.29 to 1.03. Refused interviews are now set
  aside, with a message giving the count.
- **Roving (mean-of-ratios) rates now weight each party by its size** when
  `n_anglers` is available. The estimator is defined per angler, but an
  interview is a party. Weighting parties equally leaned toward small parties'
  rates; in a simulation where larger parties caught fish faster, the old rate
  was 23% low. On the example roving data the rate moves from 0.197 to 0.191
  fish per angler-hour. Designs without `n_anglers`, or with a constant party
  size, are unchanged.
- **Catch rows with no species are refused.** They were counted in the
  all-species total and dropped from every species row, so the species rows did
  not add up to the total. Label them (for example `"unidentified"`, which is
  reported as its own species) or drop them on purpose.
- **Counts dated outside the calendar, or in the wrong stratum, are refused.**
  A count outside the calendar became a sampled day the population did not
  contain: four such counts moved a test effort estimate from 151 to 277.
- **Sectioned catch totals use the stratified sum.** Without `by`, each
  section's effort was multiplied by one rate pooled across its strata, so a
  section's total could differ from the sum of its `by = day_type` rows (by up
  to about 4% on the package fixture).
- **`summarize_cws_rates()` handles creels that record only harvest and
  release.** It read only `"caught"` rows, so such creels got a CWS of 0. On
  the example data, bass moves from 0.052 to 0.185 and walleye from 0.462 to
  0.629.

## Standard errors that change

Point estimates are unchanged in this group; the uncertainty around them moves.

- **The finite-population correction no longer erases count-timing
  uncertainty.** On season and stratum totals, a stratum where a sampled day
  had a single count could have its standard error shrunk to nothing, because
  sampling more days does not remove the uncertainty about *when in the day*
  the count fell. With every day sampled, the SE was exactly 0. On the example
  season the effort SE rises from 1,079 to 1,286 angler-hours, and every catch,
  harvest and release total built on that effort inherits the change.
- **Within-day variance is no longer counted twice** on
  `target = "sampled_days"` with two or more counts a day. On a four-day test
  fixture the SE falls from 276.9 to 100.
- **Designs with more than one strata column** (for example
  `strata = c(day_type, month)`) had their standard errors computed over the
  first column only. In one season the effort SE was 147.7 where it should have
  been 187.9.
- **Sectioned lake totals now account for sections that rise and fall
  together.** A busy day is busy in every section, and the lake total had
  treated sections as independent. In simulation, interval coverage went from
  91.5% to 94.8%.
- **The bootstrap no longer reports zero variance for a stratum with one
  sampled day.** That design is now refused, as Taylor and the jackknife
  already refused it.
- **An unknown within-day component is reported as `NA`, not `0`.** With one
  count a day, the within-day part cannot be separated out. The total SE is
  unchanged, but `se_within` now says "unknown" rather than "measured and found
  to be zero".

## The package stops instead of guessing

A theme runs through many of these changes: an unknown value is not a zero.
Where `tidycreel` used to drop something and report the rest, it now stops and
tells you what is missing:

- A stratum with effort but no catch rate (for example, no complete weekend
  trips) used to be left out of the catch total, with only a warning. On the
  package example that left out 54% of the season's effort. It now stops and
  names the cells. `missing_rate = "exclude"` is the explicit way to leave them
  out, and the result records what was excluded.
- On bus-route and ice designs, parties that were counted but not interviewed
  entered totals as zero effort and zero catch. They are now refused by name.
- A season total that would silently leave out a never-sampled stratum (a
  Labor Day stratum, say) is now refused.

If your script stops where it used to run, the error message names the problem
and the way forward.

## Less noise

Warnings have been sorted into tiers. Warnings that the estimate may be wrong
still print every time. Data-quality warnings now print once per design rather
than on every call: one season script went from 216 copies of the same warning
to one. Information that is not a warning, such as the count of zero-catch
interviews, is now a message. `get_warnings()` lists everything that was
raised on a design or an estimate.

## New in the development version

A short list. The [NEWS](https://chrischizinski.com/tidycreel/dev/news/) has
the details.

- `creel_calendar()` builds the season calendar that `creel_design()` takes.
- Night creels: schedules and designs whose survey day crosses midnight.
- `write_design()` and `read_design()` save a design and rebuild it.
- `summarize_rws_rates()` for released-while-sought rates.
- `prep_interview_totals()` builds each interview's catch, harvest and release
  totals from a long catch table, so interviews and catch can come from the
  same records.
- A new example dataset, `example_roving_interviews`.
- The [vignettes](https://chrischizinski.com/tidycreel/dev/articles/) were
  reorganized into a tutorial, how-to guides, explanations and reference, and
  checked against the code.

## What to do

- **If you use aerial designs, re-run your catch, harvest and release totals.**
- If your totals changed and you want the old numbers, add
  `target = "sampled_days"`. Then check whether the season total is what you
  meant all along.
- If you hit a new error, read it: it names the stratum, date or row involved.
- If something looks wrong, please
  [open an issue](https://github.com/chrischizinski/tidycreel/issues).

All of this is planned for the next CRAN release in December.
